description: Fix two broken API endpoints and one missing DB branch in officer_portal.py. (1) send_rejection_feedback() in bidders.py: _save_feedback() is a confirmed no-op in DB mode (lines 812-813); fix it to call db.update_rejection_feedback_db(fb_id, updates) and db.append_audit() in DB mode. Also fix bidder_rejection_feedback() which marks records as read via the same broken _save_feedback path. (2) submit_committee_score() in officer_portal.py JSON path (lines ~920-943): the JSON fallback path writes directly to bids.json and audit.json via save_json instead of using db calls, but it does NOT have a USE_DATABASE guard — the function already has a complete DB branch (lines 857-894), but the JSON path at ~895-943 still runs save_json('bids.json') and save_json('audit.json'). Confirm the DB branch is complete and unreachable duplicate JSON writes are removed/guarded. (3) conflict_declaration() in officer_portal.py (line 1141): currently JSON-only in both modes — add USE_DATABASE branch that calls db.create_conflict_declaration_db() and db.append_audit(); keep JSON path for local mode. These three fixes are independent of each other but all go in this FEAT.
steps: Step 1: Read backend/routes/bidders.py lines 800-870 fully. Confirm _save_feedback (lines ~812-813) is `if not USE_DATABASE: save_cached(...)` (no-op in DB mode). Confirm send_rejection_feedback() (line ~831) loads records, mutates them in-place, then calls _save_feedback(records). Confirm bidder_rejection_feedback() also calls _save_feedback().

Step 2: Fix _save_feedback() in backend/routes/bidders.py to add DB path: `if USE_DATABASE: db.update_rejection_feedback_db(fb_id, updates); else: save_cached('rejection_feedback.json', data)`. Because _save_feedback currently takes the whole list, restructure send_rejection_feedback() to build an updates dict {additional_feedback, feedback_sent_at, feedback_sent_by} and call db.update_rejection_feedback_db(fb_id, updates) directly in the DB branch instead of mutating the list. Keep the list-mutation + save_cached approach for the JSON branch. In DB mode also replace the direct save_cached('audit.json') audit write (inside the try block in send_rejection_feedback) with db.append_audit({...}).

Step 3: Fix bidder_rejection_feedback() in backend/routes/bidders.py (the route that marks feedback records as read/unread). Read the function, identify the _save_feedback call, and apply the same dual-mode fix: in DB mode call db.update_rejection_feedback_db(fb_id, {'read': True/False}) instead of mutating the list and calling _save_feedback.

Step 4: Read backend/routes/officer_portal.py lines 831-946 (submit_committee_score). Confirm the DB branch at lines ~857-894 is complete and calls db.append_audit(). Confirm lines ~895-943 (the JSON fallback path) calls save_json('bids.json') and save_json('audit.json') directly without a USE_DATABASE=False guard. Add `if not USE_DATABASE:` at the entry of the JSON fallback block to make it unreachable in DB mode, so the JSON writes cannot fire when USE_DATABASE is True.

Step 5: Read backend/routes/officer_portal.py conflict_declaration() function (line 1141). It currently calls load_json/save_json in both modes. Add USE_DATABASE branch: in DB mode call `db.create_conflict_declaration_db(declaration)` and `db.append_audit({...})`; in JSON mode keep the existing load_json/save_json path. Remove the incorrect comment that says 'Sprint 2 migration did not create a conflict_declarations table' (the table EXISTS in the Sprint 2 migration at line 637 of 20250719_120000_sprint2_all_entities.py). Note: db.create_conflict_declaration_db() does not exist yet — add a stub in database.py as part of this step (the full function will be completed in FEAT-002 after the migration adds columns).

Step 6: In backend/services/database.py, add stub functions create_conflict_declaration_db(data: Dict) -> Dict, list_conflict_declarations_db(filters: Dict = None) -> List[Dict], get_conflict_declaration_db(id: str) -> Optional[Dict]. These stubs will INSERT/SELECT from the conflict_declarations table using the existing column names from the Sprint 2 migration (id, tender_id, bidder_id, declared_by, declared_at, conflict_type, description, resolved, resolved_at, created_at). Map endpoint fields: officer_id -> declared_by, conflict_reason -> description, action -> conflict_type. The full column alignment (adding officer_name, has_conflict, action as separate columns) happens in FEAT-002 after the migration runs.

Step 7: Syntax-check every modified file: `python -m py_compile backend/routes/bidders.py`, `python -m py_compile backend/routes/officer_portal.py`, `python -m py_compile backend/services/database.py`.
acceptance_criteria: python -m py_compile backend/routes/bidders.py exits 0 with no errors
python -m py_compile backend/routes/officer_portal.py exits 0 with no errors
python -m py_compile backend/services/database.py exits 0 with no errors
_save_feedback() in bidders.py no longer silently discards the DB write — it calls db.update_rejection_feedback_db() in DB mode
send_rejection_feedback() uses db.append_audit() in DB mode instead of save_cached('audit.json')
submit_committee_score() JSON fallback path is guarded with `if not USE_DATABASE:` so it cannot fire in production
conflict_declaration() has a USE_DATABASE branch calling db.create_conflict_declaration_db()
db.create_conflict_declaration_db(), db.list_conflict_declarations_db(), db.get_conflict_declaration_db() exist in database.py
findings: FEAT-002 note: create_conflict_declaration_db() in database.py maps officer_id->declared_by, conflict_reason->description, action->conflict_type, and strips officer_name and has_conflict (not DB columns). If FEAT-002 adds has_conflict, officer_name, or action as separate DB columns via migration, update the field mapping in create_conflict_declaration_db() accordingly. The Sprint 2 conflict_declarations table schema is confirmed: id, tender_id, bidder_id, declared_by, declared_at, conflict_type, description, resolved, resolved_at, created_at.
